suggestions: Provide actual BP reading (e.g., '225/135 mmHg on right arm, sitting') not generic '140/90 mmHg'
Describe fundoscopy findings systematically: optic disc (swelling, blurring), retinal vessels (arteriovenous nicking, copper/silver wiring), haemorrhages, exudates, papilloedema
Include relevant imaging: CXR (cardiomegaly, pulmonary oedema), ECG (LVH with strain pattern), CT head (if neurological symptoms - exclude ICH/stroke)
Use Australian terminology: 'hypertensive retinopathy' (Keith-Wagener-Barker classification), 'papilloedema', 'flame-shaped haemorrhages'
Specify hypertensive emergency criteria: BP >180/120 mmHg WITH end-organ damage (encephalopathy, acute kidney injury, pulmonary oedema, MI, aortic dissection)
Expected answers should include: 'BP 225/135 mmHg, Grade IV hypertensive retinopathy with papilloedema and retinal haemorrhages on fundoscopy'
Differential diagnosis should consider: hypertensive emergency vs urgency, secondary hypertension causes (phaeochromocytoma, renal artery stenosis), acute aortic dissection
Management: IV antihypertensives (labetalol, hydralazine), target BP reduction 10-20% in first hour, admit to HDU/ICU, investigate end-organ damage
Replace generic RAG references with relevant Australian guidelines: National Heart Foundation (hypertension management), RANZCR (fundoscopy imaging), eTG (hypertensive emergency treatment)
strengths: OSCE structure is appropriate (3 tasks: interpretation, differential, management)
10-minute duration is realistic for imaging interpretation station
Includes two relevant investigations (BP measurement + fundoscopy) for hypertensive emergency assessment

detailed_analysis.systematic_approach_assessment: FAIL - No systematic radiological interpretation demonstrated. For fundoscopy, should use: (1) Optic disc assessment (margins, colour, cup-to-disc ratio), (2) Retinal vessels (AV ratio, arteriovenous nicking, tortuosity), (3) Macula (foveal reflex, exudates), (4) Periphery (haemorrhages, cotton-wool spots). For hypertensive emergency, must document Keith-Wagener-Barker grade. This OSCE provides NO actual findings - only generic statements.
detailed_analysis.australian_terminology_assessment: PARTIAL - Uses 'Hypertensive Emergency' (correct Australian/international term) but image descriptions are non-specific. Should include: 'Grade IV hypertensive retinopathy', 'papilloedema', 'flame-shaped haemorrhages', 'cotton-wool spots', 'macular star exudate'. Vital signs show BP 140/90 mmHg which does NOT meet hypertensive emergency criteria (requires >180/120 mmHg).
detailed_analysis.clinical_relevance_assessment: FAIL - Content is template-generated with no clinically relevant details. A real hypertensive emergency OSCE should describe: (1) Actual BP reading (e.g., 225/135 mmHg), (2) Symptoms (headache, visual disturbance, chest pain, dyspnoea), (3) Fundoscopy findings (specific grade of retinopathy, presence/absence of papilloedema), (4) End-organ damage evidence (AKI with Cr 380 µmol/L, pulmonary oedema on CXR, troponin elevation). This OSCE provides NONE of these details.
detailed_analysis.image_quality_assessment: INADEQUATE - No assessment of: (1) BP measurement technique (correct cuff size? patient position? multiple readings?), (2) Fundoscopy image quality (pupil dilatation? clear media? adequate view of disc and macula?), (3) Technical adequacy for diagnostic interpretation. Real OSCE should note if fundoscopy limited by media opacity (cataract) or inadequate pupil dilatation.
detailed_analysis.educational_value: LOW - This OSCE appears to be template-generated without actual medical content. It would not adequately prepare AMC candidates for real imaging interpretation stations. Candidate would receive no practice in: (1) Systematic fundoscopy interpretation, (2) Hypertensive retinopathy grading, (3) Differentiating hypertensive emergency vs urgency, (4) Correlating imaging findings with clinical severity.
